clue.text: Fuel prejudice about orgy, oddly

indicators.note: one thing set about another surrounds it, so the word for prejudice wraps round what follows
oddly asks for the letters in odd positions only, first, third and so on

blocks.note: bias is a prejudice
first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone objects to fuel on the grounds that its makers seem rather too fond of wild parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Biogas is gas such as methane made by rotting organic matter, burned as a fuel.

clue.text: Get dog at home, to start with

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Advice to acquire a dog that will begin by living indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' places the at-home word at the front, before the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it upon yourself, that is, to get it.

clue.text: Information on old American city

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
O is a standard abbreviation for old
A abbreviates American

explanation.surface: Someone seeks details about an old American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the pieces one after another; 'old American city' looks like a single phrase, but only 'city' is the definition and the place is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major port city in north-west Italy, birthplace of Columbus.

clue.text: Saw guards beginning to like killing

indicators.note: something that guards another keeps it enclosed within itself
the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: a saw is an old proverb or saying
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An observer notes guards starting to enjoy a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past of see, but here it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaying is a literary or journalistic word for murdering or killing someone.

clue.text: Son and second daughter abandoning hopeless witness

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so those letters are dropped from the next word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
D abbreviates daughter; it is the second D in the word that goes
despondent means without hope

explanation.surface: A son and daughter walk out on a witness who has given up hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DESPONDENT, remove its S and its second D, and DEPONENT is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A deponent is a legal term for someone who gives sworn evidence, usually in a written statement.

clue.text: Dance record on vacation creates division

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outer shell

blocks.note: a disco is a dance
outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Playing a dance record while on holiday starts a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is disagreement or strife, a division between people.

clue.text: Publications about masculine pets

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: newspapers are publications
M is the grammar abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: Magazines devoted to male animals kept as pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like a noun but is the verb: to pet is to indulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to indulge and fuss over them, just as one pets a favourite.

clue.text: No red meat cooked in place of worship

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been prepared and transformed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule that no red meat may be cooked in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great Gothic cathedral in Paris, a famous Christian place of worship.

clue.text: Revolutionary study protects pests? It doesn't matter

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for study runs backwards
something that protects another shields it by surrounding it

blocks.note: a den is a private study
vermin are pests

explanation.surface: A radical research project shelters pests, and the clue shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'pests?' look like a query, but the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind is an everyday phrase telling someone not to worry because something is unimportant.

clue.text: Outrages Conservative, wearing attire showing a bit of skin

indicators.note: the wearer is inside the clothing, so this letter sits within the attire

blocks.clueFragment: attire showing a bit of skin
blocks.note: open shoes that leave much of the foot bare
C abbreviates Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is outraged by revealing clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bit of skin' suggests racy clothes, but sandals show only toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandals are shocking events or actions that cause public outrage, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Second time Eccles has to give ground

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
T is the abbreviation for time
the setter Eccles says 'I've', meaning I have

explanation.surface: The setter, Eccles, is asked a second time to concede ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give ground' looks like retreating, but 'ground' alone is the noun meaning a reason. A setter often refers to themself by name, so 'Eccles has' is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason or grounds for doing something.

clue.text: Forlorn nurse is drilling head

indicators.note: a drill bores into something, so these words go inside the word for head

blocks.note: to nurse a child is to rear it
taken as written
dome is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A sad nurse is boring into someone's skull, a grim scene of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearisome is an old-fashioned variant of dreary, meaning gloomy, cheerless and forlorn.

clue.text: Country, before India invades

indicators.note: an invader goes into territory, so this letter enters the other word

blocks.note: ere is a poetic word for before
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A nation is described as existing before India invades it.
explanation.definitionFit: Éire is the Irish-language name for the Republic of Ireland, a European nation.

clue.text: Relieved idiot carried on broadcast

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard rather than read, so the result is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
to wage a war is to carry it on

explanation.surface: A fool, relieved, kept talking on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'ass waged' runs together to sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuaged means eased or soothed, as pain or worry is relieved.

clue.text: Descends on eccentric who provides presentation

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to slide is to go down smoothly
letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball comes down to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply strings the parts together.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide show is a presentation of images projected one after another.

clue.text: Ireland and US: works in progress

indicators.note: the letters are worked, that is, processed and reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both names; 'and' joins them

explanation.surface: A report that Irish and American projects are underway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works in progress' reads as one phrase, but 'works' is the signal and the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship under sail is moving with its sails set, so figuratively it means underway or in progress.

clue.text: Despot's drug left for later time

indicators.note: one thing for another means one stands in place of the other

blocks.note: statins are cholesterol-lowering drugs
L is the abbreviation for left
T for time; 'later' picks the second of its two Ts

explanation.surface: A tyrant's medication is put off until later.
explanation.walkthrough: Put L in place of the second T of STATIN to get STALIN; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator, the archetypal despot.

clue.text: Stokes stopping Broad and Anderson finally producing their bible

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside
finally points to the very last letter of the name

blocks.note: broad means wide
S is a symbol for the stokes, a unit of viscosity
last letter of the name

explanation.surface: England cricketers Ben Stokes, Stuart Broad and James Anderson produce the book cricketers revere.
explanation.walkthrough: The three names are all England Test cricketers, so the surface stays in cricket; the definition's 'their' refers back to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisden Cricketers' Almanack is the annual reference book known as the bible of cricket.

clue.text: Bloke at entrance turned round to show piece of identification

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a man posted at a gate is a gateman

explanation.surface: A doorman turns round to display his ID badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge worn to identify the wearer by name.

clue.text: Predict that man gets terribly sad where a miracle occurred

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: to bet on something is to predict it
the pronoun for that man
letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecast that a man will become miserable at a holy site.
explanation.definitionFit: At the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, the Gospel of John says Jesus healed a paralysed man.

clue.text: Sat around after dance and put on weight

indicators.note: letters moved around are put in a different order

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sat about after dancing and gained some pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the dance first. 'put on weight' looks like getting fatter but means loading a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To ballast a ship is to load it with heavy material for stability, i.e. to add weight.

clue.text: Goes up and down, sharing new vegetables

indicators.note: in a down entry, one word is read upwards, backwards, while the other runs down normally
two words sharing a letter overlap on it, so one copy of the letter for new is dropped

blocks.note: a go is a turn, read in the down direction
a go is also a spin, as in taking a car for a spin

explanation.surface: Something bobs up and down while sharing out fresh produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' does double duty, giving two words for a go; one is reversed and they overlap on N, the abbreviation for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips are root vegetables with white flesh, plural to match the clue's plural noun.

clue.text: Tackle good listener

blocks.note: G abbreviates good
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An order to confront a good listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb but is the noun for equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is equipment, as in fishing tackle, which is another word for gear.

clue.text: Abused whisky and responded heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: malt is a kind of whisky
to react is to respond

explanation.surface: Someone mistreated with drink answered without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: REACTED loses its middle letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat cruelly or badly, so maltreated means abused.

clue.text: Exposed male member creates distress

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A man exposing himself causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is fear or anxious concern, a state of distress.

clue.text: Mathematician and European leader wanting introduction

indicators.note: lacking its introduction means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: E abbreviates European
a ruler is a leader

explanation.surface: A mathematician and a European head of state who needs to be introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician, one of the most prolific ever.

clue.text: Stop plugging uncouth war tunes

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, here sitting inside the following words

blocks.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A call to stop promoting crude military songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' poses as advertising songs, but the answer is held inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart is to prevent someone achieving something, to stop them.

clue.text: Aim to slip lead in cordial

indicators.note: letters that slip out of place end up in a new order

blocks.note: letters rearranged
an electrical lead is a cable

explanation.surface: Trying to slip a dog's lead into a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective for friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable and cordial both describe relations that are friendly and good-natured.

clue.text: Is going to cut short boring drunk just after sunset

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off
boring into something means drilling inside it

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
will expresses the future, 'is going to'

explanation.surface: A dull drunk will be sent away early, after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is going to' is the future auxiliary, not a verb of motion; 'boring' means dull on the surface but drilling here.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the soft half-light in the period immediately after the sun goes down.

clue.text: Morose Mexican's hat, 25% off

indicators.note: a quarter off means a quarter of the letters, from the end, are taken away

blocks.note: the wide-brimmed Mexican hat

explanation.surface: A gloomy Mexican's hat is being sold at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight letters less a quarter leaves six: the last two go.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and gloomy in mood, so it matches morose.
